reasoning_traces.think:
Zhang’s FCI rules R5–R10 govern causal edge orientation in the presence of latent variables. R5 handles circle cycles, R10 completes tails based on uncovered paths. The original implementation suffered from iteration-order dependence and rule interference. The fix introduced in pcalg and adopted here involves structurally isolating rule application via an optional rules parameter. This ensures deterministic outcomes per test case. The mutation sweep validates that each rule is uniquely pinned by its test. Failure to fail indicates competing rules (e.g., R8 vs. completeAncestral) produce identical outputs, masking rule specificity. The structural change aligns with pcalg’s established pattern, ensuring correctness and reproducibility in causal discovery pipelines.
